fact_text: Lower global oil prices help Pakistan by easing inflation, which lets interest rates fall and supports higher stock market valuations.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rough rule of thumb is that a $10 fall in oil lifts the market P/E by about one multiple point, working through lower inflation and interest rates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil, coal, gas and steel are the basic inputs behind most goods, and Pakistan is a large importer of them, so falling prices for these four cut its import bill.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When a global slowdown reduces demand, commodity prices tend to fall, which benefits commodity-importing economies such as Pakistan more than it hurts them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Higher import tariffs raise prices and cut buying power, which lowers production and commodity demand; the analyst saw this chain as positive for Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Falling interest rates make stocks more attractive than bank deposits, which tends to raise the P/E multiples investors are willing to pay.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst backtested a rough rule that the market P/E should sit near 20 minus the prevailing interest rate, which he said fit Pakistan well.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A national default does not by itself close the stock market; it mainly blocks import letters of credit, hurting import-dependent firms, while fear pushes prices down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Businesses holding dollar-linked assets, such as factories, tend to keep their value as the rupee devalues, so the analyst favoured asset ownership as protection against inflation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treated the gap between market price and estimated fair value as the decisive test, finding a stock priced well below fair value an attractive candidate.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fair value methods give broadly similar answers, so the result depends mainly on the quality of assumptions about future profits and on understanding the business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A P/E is reliable for an individual company only after its earnings are normalised for one-off items, other income and tax-rate effects, and the normalisation differs by sector.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A P/E works better on a whole index than on one company, because one company's unusual earnings year averages out across many companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Bank earnings depend on interest rates, so when rates fall a bank's future earnings can shrink and the market may refuse to pay its current P/E.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Book value reflects what a company's assets cost, while market price reflects the earnings those assets can produce, so a low book value does not by itself make a stock cheap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argued that a shareholder receives the same share of profits as the business owner, while a property buyer does not share in the developer's margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Many retail investors do not know a stock's fair value, so they sell on falls and on rallies alike, which the analyst saw as a common source of losses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sui Southern Gas earns from the gas it sells, but the government sets an allowed level of unaccounted-for gas, and losses beyond that level are absorbed by the company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst called Sui Southern Gas highly volatile because its gas-loss control varies by region, with Balochistan losses a major issue, and suggested only detailed researchers hold it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expected Sui Southern Gas to begin paying dividends from FY26, as the company had reportedly stated in its corporate briefing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Rally !! Special session' (YouTube transcript, undated)
